title: Two-Pass Texture Enhancement and Creative Dodge on Iceberg Imagery (Dehaze, Crop, Blur)

date.basis: embedded_creation_time in metadata; folder naming indicates 2026 session

summary: The video documents a hands-on editing session focused on ice/water imagery. The speaker describes processing a hole shot in two ways (unmodified and with heavy dehaze to reveal textures), then moves through cropping, applying dehaze again with added clarity and brightness, and experimentations on an iceberg top. A recurring theme is using dodging to shape shadows into an eye-like band and blending it into the composition. The session also demonstrates dirt removal from water using the blur tool, edge-blending with soft brushes, and reintroducing the original texture to avoid over-editing. The narrator discusses exposure and white adjustments, noting how dehaze can create striking, abstract results in otherwise ordinary frames.

sections.title: Dodging shadows to create emphasis and a band

sections.title: Removing water dirt with blur and careful blending
sections.description: Dirt in the water is removed using the blur tool at an appropriate strength, then edges are softened and blended with the surrounding area; the original texture is painted back as needed.

sections.title: Finishing touches: exposure notes, color and final texture decisions
sections.description: The session concludes with refinements such as adjusting exposure and white levels, balancing blues, applying hard-edge corrections, and reintroducing original textures to avoid over-editing.
